video:video.video:description: Foreign ministers from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, joined by counterparts from China, Japan and South Korea, gathered in Manila on Thursday for a family photo and the traditional ASEAN handshake after a series of regional meetings.

video:video.video:description: A replica of the House of the Virgin Mary in the Philippines welcomes devotees in Asia’s largest Catholic nation.

video:video.video:title: U.S. military says it conducted 13th night of strikes against Iran

video:video.video:title: Giant metal roosters spread autism acceptance in Maine after town zoning spat
video:video.video:description: Giant metal roosters are popping up on lawns in and around a coastal Maine community and as far away as New Zealand in support of a 6-year-old autistic girl and her love of the colorful creations.

video:video.video:description: The police shooting death of a homeless man who wounded an officer with a knife while resisting arrest has roiled Wisconsin's capital city, with protesters and community groups demanding accountability and an end to racial injustice.

video:video.video:description: Nicaragua moved to eliminate elections this week, marking the latest step in President Daniel Ortega's yearslong consolidation of power after he declared the country would no longer hold votes and lawmakers began advancing constitutional changes to carry out the plan.

video:video.video:description: Estonia's Kirikla Orthodox Monastery is the first of its kind to be established by the Estonian Apostolic Orthodox Church in decades.

video:video.video:description: The beaches in Nigeria's megacity of Lagos are rare public spaces to escape the crowds and heat, but many residents say they are being priced out as the local government opens up more coastal land to developers.
